title: Message contracts and envelopes
summary: What a message promises: the envelope (id, type, version, correlation, time), CloudEvents as the standard, and where metadata lives in RabbitMQ and Kafka.

steps.title: A message is a contract
body: The broker does not care what is in a message: Kafka stores bytes, RabbitMQ routes bytes. The **contract** lives
between the teams: the shape of the data, what each field means, and the metadata every consumer can rely on.
Split every message into an **envelope** (facts about the message) and **data** (facts about the business event):
│ id            e-91                    unique per message: dedup key  │
│ type          shop.order.placed.v2    picks the handler and schema   │
│ correlationid c-77                    the business flow it belongs to│
│ causationid   e-90                    the message that caused this   │
Why bother: a consumer can dedup, route, trace and pick a deserializer **without parsing the data**, and you can
change the data's shape while the envelope stays stable.
> **Try it:** in **Labs → Live network labs → 25 Live Kafka lab**, produce a v1 and a v2 payload to the same topic
> with `kafka-console-producer.sh --reader-property parse.key=true --reader-property key.separator=:` and read them back. The
> broker accepts both without a word: nothing but your contract and your registry stops a breaking change.

steps.title: CloudEvents and where metadata lives
body: **CloudEvents 1.0** (a CNCF standard) names these attributes so every team and tool agrees: required `specversion`
(`correlationid`) must be **lowercase letters and digits only**. Azure Event Grid, Knative and many SDKs speak it.
- **Structured mode**: the whole event, envelope plus `data`, is one JSON document in the body.
- **Binary mode**: the body is just the data; attributes travel as headers (`ce_type` in Kafka, `ce-type` in HTTP).
Setting the envelope with the real clients:
await channel.BasicPublishAsync("orders", "order.eu.placed", mandatory: true, basicProperties: props, body: body);

explain: `type[..dot]` is everything before the last dot, and `dot + 2` skips the `.v`. `time` is optional in CloudEvents,
so a consumer must cope with it missing, which is the first taste of a **tolerant reader**.

steps.title: Wrap the event
prompt: Write `string Wrap(string id, string source, string type, string correlationId, string dataJson, DateTimeOffset occurredAt)`
that returns a **structured-mode CloudEvent** as compact JSON, with the properties in exactly this order:
- `time` is `occurredAt` converted to UTC, formatted `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ` (for example `2026-11-26T14:05:12Z`).
- `data` is the parsed `dataJson` embedded as JSON (an object, not a string).
starter: string Wrap(string id, string source, string type, string correlationId, string dataJson, DateTimeOffset occurredAt)
solution: string Wrap(string id, string source, string type, string correlationId, string dataJson, DateTimeOffset occurredAt)
hints: An anonymous object serializes its properties in declaration order: `new { specversion = "1.0", id, source, ... }`.
`JsonDocument.Parse(dataJson).RootElement` serializes as the JSON it holds.
template: Dojo.Check("data is embedded as an object, not a string", Wrap("e", "/s", "t.v1", "c", "{\"a\":1}", DateTimeOffset.UnixEpoch).EndsWith("\"data\":{\"a\":1}}"), "data should be JSON, not an escaped string");

steps.title: Validate incoming envelopes
prompt: The platform team wants a gate in front of the shared `events` topic. Write `string Validate(string json)` that
returns `"ok"` or the **first** problem, checking in this order:
1. not valid JSON, or not a JSON object → `"not a JSON object"`
2. each of `specversion`, `id`, `source`, `type` (in that order) missing, not a string, or empty → `"missing {name}"`
4. any top-level attribute name except `data` and `data_base64` that is not only lowercase letters and digits
5. `type` not ending in `.v` plus digits (the team's versioning convention) → `"type has no version: {type}"`
6. `time` present but not a string that parses as a date and time → `"time is not a timestamp"`
solution: if (root.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.Object) return "not a JSON object";
if (!root.TryGetProperty(name, out var v) || v.ValueKind != JsonValueKind.String || v.GetString() == "")
hints: Parse inside `try { ... } catch (JsonException)`, then check `RootElement.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Object`.
`Regex.IsMatch(p.Name, "^[a-z0-9]+$")` for attribute names, `Regex.IsMatch(type, @"\.v[0-9]+$")` for the version.
`DateTimeOffset.TryParse(text, CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, DateTimeStyles.None, out _)` checks the time.
template: Dojo.Eq("not JSON", "not a JSON object", Validate("order placed"));
Dojo.Eq("a JSON array", "not a JSON object", Validate("[1,2]"));
Dojo.Eq("required attributes are checked in order", "missing specversion", Validate("""{"type":"x"}"""));
Dojo.Eq("data's own field names are not checked", "ok", Validate("""{"specversion":"1.0","id":"e-1","source":"/orders-api","type":"shop.order.placed.v2","data":{"orderId":"o-7"}}"""));
Dojo.Eq("unversioned type", "type has no version: shop.order.placed", Validate("""{"specversion":"1.0","id":"e-1","source":"/orders-api","type":"shop.order.placed"}"""));
Dojo.Eq("bad time", "time is not a timestamp", Validate("""{"specversion":"1.0","id":"e-1","source":"/orders-api","type":"shop.order.placed.v1","time":"yesterday"}"""));
